question: Which choice most logically completes the text? In people, right-handedness is vastly more common than left-handedness. Turning to nonhuman primates, a 1995 investigation of wild orangutans by Lesley J. Rogers and Gisela Kaplan detected no bias toward the right hand, whereas a 1991 investigation of captive chimpanzees by S.G. Lutz-Maki and P.F. MacNeilage did find such a bias. That chimpanzee study, however, examined just 14 animals, and a meta-analysis of primate-handedness research concludes that, to statistically justify a claim that a group displays handedness at the population level, a study must include at least 176 individuals—implying that ______
option a: the apparent difference between the two studies' results may be partly attributable to the 1991 study using a different standard to determine handedness than the 1995 study did.
option b: any right-handedness exhibited by captive chimpanzees might be an effect of extended contact with humans.
option c: the population size in the study that did not report right-handedness in orangutans is too small to justify that conclusion.
option d: the population size in the study that reported right-handedness in chimpanzees is too small to justify that conclusion.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: With only 14 chimpanzees, the 1991 study falls far short of the 176-individual threshold needed to claim population-level handedness.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Opening at San Francisco International Airport in February 2002, the exhibit Sacred Havens: A Quiet Space of Gardens showcased a curated selection of ______ a bit more visual interest to the hustle and bustle of the terminals.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A comma with the participial phrase "adding" correctly attaches the modifier to the main clause.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? A member of the celebrated African American quiltmaking community of Gee's Bend, ______
option a: the 1960s was when Beatrice Pettway crafted a quilt called Work-Clothes Quilt that was acquired by a Kentucky art museum.
option b: Beatrice Pettway crafted a quilt in the 1960s called Work-Clothes Quilt that was acquired by a Kentucky art museum.
option c: a quilt called Work-Clothes Quilt was crafted by Beatrice Pettway in the 1960s and acquired by a Kentucky art museum.
option d: a Kentucky art museum acquired a quilt called Work-Clothes Quilt that was crafted by Beatrice Pettway in the 1960s.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Only choice B places "Beatrice Pettway" directly after the introductory modifier describing her.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Indian American composer Reena Esmail wrote the classical work "Teen Murti." Blending Western classical music with Raag Malkauns—a melodic framework from Hindustani classical music that conjures a somber mood—this composition ______ Esmail's cross-cultural sensibility as a composer.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The sentence needs the finite main verb "exemplifies" to be complete.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Covering the territory around what is today Elista, Russia, the Kalmyk-speaking Kalmyk Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic was a region of the Soviet Union that held autonomy in name only. By enabling the Kalmyk Republic and other Soviet republics drawn along ethnolinguistic lines to assert their prerogatives, the reforms of President Mikhail Gorbachev ______ to the Soviet Union's breakup.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: "contributed" supplies the finite main verb the subject "the reforms" requires.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? In a 2024 study, researchers gauging the tree biodiversity of Amsterdam began by tallying the number of trees across different parts of the city. They found that administrative unit GK13 contained 5,179 trees. ______ administrative unit GM14 held only 12.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: "In contrast" fits the sharp drop from 5,179 trees to just 12.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? Ecologists like Michelle Evans-White rely on the trophic pyramid to depict how energy moves through an ecosystem via food. Primary producers such as algae sit at the pyramid's base and feed herbivores such as shrimp at the second trophic level; those animals, ______ feed omnivores and carnivores such as seals at the third level; and so the pattern continues up the food chain.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: "in turn" conveys the successive transfer of energy up the pyramid.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? In 1997 the Advanced Composition Explorer satellite, a craft that studies solar wind and cosmic rays, held an orbit at the Sun-Earth L1 Lagrange point—a spot lying directly between Earth and the Sun. ______ the gravitational pulls of the Sun and Earth balance out, an equilibrium found in very few other places that lets spacecraft such as the Advanced Composition Explorer keep the same position relative to Earth as they orbit the Sun.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: "There" points back to the L1 point just described.

question: The student wants to place the finding of Slotte's team's study in the context of the 2023 review. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal? While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes: The growth-survival paradigm (GSP) holds that faster-growing fish larvae have higher rates of survival to maturity than slower-growing larvae do. Aril Slotte et al. (2019) tested whether the GSP applies to cohorts of Atlantic herring (Clupea harengus). Finding: slower-growing C. harengus larvae survived at a significantly higher rate than comparatively fast-growing C. harengus larvae. Dominique Robert et al. (2023) surveyed 153 GSP studies published between 1971 and 2022, including Slotte's team's study. Robert et al.: "The GSP was supported in the majority of cases," but a "non-negligible proportion of reviewed studies demonstrated the occurrence of selection [favoring] slow-growing individuals in the field, a possibility generally disregarded in the...GSP."
option a: Demonstrating that slower-growing larvae had a survival advantage over faster-growing larvae, Slotte's team's finding regarding C. harengus was consistent with those of the majority of studies included in the review.
option b: Presenting evidence of differing survival rates among C. harengus larvae, Slotte's team's study reinforces the review's contention that the GSP's applicability to slower-growing larvae tends to be overlooked.
option c: Reporting survival outcomes among C. harengus larvae that contradict the GSP's predictions, Slotte's team's study is one of several in the review that highlight the paradigm's limitations.
option d: Suggesting the absence of a relationship between growth rates and survival outcomes, Slotte's team's study of C. harengus larvae is among those in the review that undermine the GSP.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Slotte's contrary result exemplifies the minority of reviewed studies showing the GSP's limits.

question: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between Marianne Moore and Edith Wharton. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal? While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes: A copyright bars a book's contents from being reproduced (published) without the copyright holder's permission. When a book's copyright expires, the work enters the public domain and anyone may legally reproduce it. Observations is a poetry collection by Marianne Moore; it entered the public domain in 2020. The Mother's Recompense is a novel by Edith Wharton; it entered the public domain in 2021.
option a: Both Observations and The Mother's Recompense are in the public domain; however, one is a poetry collection and the other a novel.
option b: Marianne Moore and Edith Wharton are two authors whose works recently entered the public domain.
option c: Observations, a poetry collection by Marianne Moore, entered the public domain in 2020, unlike Edith Wharton's novel The Mother's Recompense.
option d: The year was 2021, and the copyright to Edith Wharton's The Mother's Recompense had finally expired.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Choice B highlights the shared fact that both authors' works recently entered the public domain.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Opening at San Francisco International Airport in January 2004, the exhibit Go Hawaiʻi: Airline Posters presented a curated selection of ______ a bit more visual interest to the hustle and bustle of the terminals.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A comma plus the participle "adding" properly links the modifier to the main clause.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? Reaching back at least to the Middle Ages, contrafacta—works that set brand-new lyrics to the structure of an existing song—have long been common vehicles for advancing religious and political causes in popular song. ______ comic songs such as "Weird Al" Yankovic's "Spam" (a contrafactum of R.E.M.'s 1989 hit "Stand") show that humor and satire have played a parallel yet equally potent role in the contrafactum tradition.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: "By contrast" signals the shift from earnest causes to humorous, satirical use.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? Hawaii's literature is frequently described as having ______ the traditional stories of the Native Hawaiian people. Growing out of those stories, Hawaii's distinctive literary identity has since been further developed and shaped by writers such as Anwei Skinsnes Law and Gary Pak.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: "begun with" fits literature that originated in the traditional stories.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? The fossil record lets us identify species such as the western bison, an animal that ranged from Alaska to Minnesota before going extinct around 3000 BCE. Present counts of species that died out in this period, however, are probably too low, since most extinct animals are thought to be ______: many scientists believe hundreds of species from this era remain undiscovered.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: "unknown" matches the idea that hundreds of species remain undiscovered.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? Sorting authors into distinct literary movements often leads literary scholars to miss the subtleties of an individual author's style. Scholars studying the works of Henry David Thoreau, for instance, might unintentionally ______ nuances in his writing by attending only to the most obvious ways his style aligns with transcendentalism.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: "disregard" fits overlooking nuances by focusing only on the obvious traits.

question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text? Mexican textile artist Victoria Villasana tells stories of triumph through a signature technique in which she applies vivid yarn to photographs of people. In some pieces she celebrates cultural icons who are people of color, as in her depiction of the artist Frida Kahlo. In other pieces, though, she honors ordinary individuals, as in her captivating portrayal of a street musician holding a guitar. Villasana views both approaches as ways of conveying the power and interconnectedness shared by all people.
option a: It provides details about Villasana's artworks, discusses specific examples of her work, and relates them to one of her artistic goals.
option b: It introduces Villasana's cultural background, describes how this background influences her art, and then outlines some of her ideas for future projects.
option c: It explains how yarn has historically been used in art, details how Villasana uses yarn in her artworks, and then comments on the popularity of her work.
option d: It compares Villasana to other contemporary artists, indicates how two of her works are similar, and then emphasizes Villasana's enthusiasm for artistic collaboration.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The text describes her works, gives examples, and ties them to one of her artistic goals.

question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text? Ethicist Ingrid Robeyns regards the use of tax havens—territories such as Switzerland that offer low tax rates to investors who live elsewhere—as a form of tax avoidance that, while legally permitted, may be morally illegitimate when investors use it to dodge contributing to the upkeep of government. Economist Gabriel Zucman finds that 8% of the world's household wealth is held in tax havens. Zucman also finds that reliance on tax havens varies by country: investors living in South Korea rarely use them, whereas many who do use them live in Argentina or Venezuela.
option a: It describes an argument made by one scholar regarding economic policy, then uses the research of a second scholar to point out flaws in that argument.
option b: It makes a claim about what constitutes profitable investment based on the research of one scholar, then uses a second scholar's findings to support that claim.
option c: It recounts how a scholar came to hold that a particular economic behavior is morally indefensible, then details the results of a study by a second scholar that lend credence to that position.
option d: It offers one scholar's opinion of an economic mechanism, then presents a second scholar's findings concerning the prevalence of that mechanism's use.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The passage gives Robeyns's opinion of tax havens, then Zucman's findings on how widely they are used.

question: Which statement about bird population responses to restoration activities in the Colorado River Delta is best supported by the text? Agricultural development in the Colorado River Delta has degraded habitat in ways harmful to native birds. When Eduardo González-Sargas et al. monitored how bird populations responded to recent efforts by the Mexican and US governments to revitalize the Delta, they recorded gains overall, though the trends varied at the species level. Populations of many native forest specialists, including Gila woodpeckers, showed signs of rebounding, while those of non-native habitat generalists, such as Eurasian collared doves, declined—trends that, though divergent, both point to habitat recovery.
option a: The fact that populations of some species have been adversely affected by restoration activities doesn't necessarily suggest that those activities have been unsuccessful.
option b: The causes of the observed divergent species-specific responses to restoration activities likely require further study to account for.
option c: Though the conservationists managing habitat restoration activities in the Colorado River Delta didn't intend to target populations of Gila woodpeckers and Eurasian collared doves, the outcomes for those species are nevertheless encouraging.
option d: Though trends in the overall bird population in response to restoration activities were initially promising, some declines observed at the species level illustrate that further adjustments to restoration plans may be required.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Adverse effects on some species do not mean the restoration efforts failed, since the declines still indicate habitat recovery.

question: Which quotation from Lady Windermere's Fan most effectively illustrates the claim? First staged in 1892, Oscar Wilde's play Lady Windermere's Fan includes a moment in which Lady Windermere regrets that she has gained certain knowledge too late for it to be of any use: ______
option a: "Actions are the first tragedy in life, words are the second. Words are perhaps the worst."
option b: "Oh, what a lesson! and what a pity that in life we only get our lessons when they are of no use to us!"
option c: "Yes, I'm of age to-day. Quite an important day in my life, isn't it?"
option d: "You are right--you are terribly right. But where am I to turn?"
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The quotation laments that lessons in life arrive only when they are no longer useful.

question:
Based on the information in the text and the table, the two students most likely disagree about the answer to which question?
Value, Cost, and Seigniorage of US Coins by Denomination, 2023
Denomination | Total value of units produced (in millions of dollars) | Gross cost (in millions of dollars) | Seigniorage (in millions of dollars) | Seigniorage per $1 issued (dollars)
One-cent | 41.4 | 127.4 | -86.0 | -2.08
Five-cent | 70.8 | 163.4 | -92.6 | -1.31
Ten-cent | 266.6 | 141.1 | 125.5 | 0.47
Quarter-dollar | 568.4 | 264.4 | 304.0 | 0.53
For Denmark's government, minting a kroner coin generates positive seigniorage—the profit earned when a coin's face value exceeds the cost of producing it—which can then help fund services such as education. Some countries, such as Finland, have stopped making certain coins because producing them yielded negative seigniorage. Discussing the table's data in an economics class, one student contends that the one-cent coin was the least financially sensible coin for the US to produce in 2023, while another maintains that the five-cent coin was.
option a: If issuing a given coin results in positive seigniorage per dollar but not as much positive seigniorage per dollar as issuing a different coin does, does it make financial sense to continue issuing the first coin?
option b: When evaluating the financial implications of issuing a coin, which is more important, the total seigniorage from issuing that coin or the seigniorage per dollar when issuing that coin?
option c: If issuing a given coin results in negative seigniorage per dollar issued, can that be changed to positive seigniorage per dollar issued by reducing the cost of issuing the coin?
option d: When determining whether it makes financial sense to issue a given coin, which is more important, the total value of the units of that coin produced or the gross cost of issuing that coin?
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The students disagree over whether total seigniorage or seigniorage per dollar is the better measure.
